name: Dzmitry Okafor-Szilvási
subcategory: augmented combat sports / APEX IRON veteran
description: A Belarusian-Nigerian heavyweight who dominated the APEX IRON league from 2183 to 2191 with a brutalist style built around HelixCorp-sponsored hydraulic shoulder assemblies and a military-grade pain-suppression BCI. His 2189 championship run — eleven consecutive knockouts including the infamous 'Spire Bout' broadcast live to all tiers — made him a cross-tier celebrity icon whose chrome-plated face became the most reproduced image in Meridian's illegal poster markets. He retired at thirty-four after catastrophic joint failure in both synthetic knees, a condition his sponsors quietly settled out of public record.
story_hooks: A sports journalist digging into the 2191 BCI scandal discovers that the missing auditor left encrypted files pointing to a broader HelixCorp program of illegal combat augmentation in at least twelve active athletes.

Okafor-Szilvási, now living in a Tier 2 care facility with failing synthetic joints, is approached by an underground fight promoter who claims HelixCorp has a prototype repair kit — but only available in exchange for one last sanctioned bout.

A Tier 1 teenager idolizes Okafor-Szilvási and undergoes black-market chrome installation to replicate his look, triggering a cascade failure that pulls the player characters into the gray-market augmentation supply chain.
